- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in the following period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias for days 1–7.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–0.3+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by 0.5–1% per step.
